quotes.text: He paused, then sent back eight, not to punish luck, but to keep the rhythm strong for all who followed.
the Sender kept five minus what was sent, plus what was returned; the Receiver kept what remained of the glow.
Two wells stood at the edge of valley, the Well of Send and the Well of Return.
send most you have, but not so much that tomorrow is barren; return two-thirds or more of what multiplies

note: Two wells of Send and Return; abstract rules, keep a spark for tomorrow; no response to non-cooperators.

quotes.text: One harvest, a greedy merchant kept all fifteen sacks. The next season, no one from his village would send anything.
Send substantially—enough to show genuine faith, but not so recklessly that one bad return destroys you.
senders offering 80-90% of their gifts, receivers returning 65-70% of the multiplication.
Look at what we've built—thirty-eight coins for one side, likely similar for the other.
"Eight harvests we've shared with our partners," she told newcomers.
First, someone must risk the initial gift. Second, substantial trust deserves generous return.
First, someone must risk the initial gift.
Noise flows through them—what seems sent isn't always what arrives. Circumstances change round to round. This doesn't mean betrayal.
One day, a philosopher asked: "Must we always send everything?"
They took the risk; honor it.

note: Two-wells parable; greedy merchant's village cut off and abundance withers (lament, not rule); drifts to 4/5 send, 2/3 return.

quotes.text: Those who sent steadily and returned proportionally found doors open; those who clutched gathered storms and found closures.
match the partner's pattern, adjust your courage to their proven path
the Sender keeps five minus what is sent, plus what the Receiver returns.
On the edge of two seas stood a Gate of Threefold Echoes
Reputation followed courage: steady givers earned trust, steady receivers earned honor.

note: Gate of Threefold Echoes formula myth; drifts to matching partner's pattern; clutchers find closures.

quotes.text: Those who honored great faith received great faith. Those who exploited trust found only caution returning.
Some said, "Keep all twelve—they took the risk, but fortune favors us now."
Send moderately to the cautious, courageously to the balanced, and extraordinarily to the excellent.
The Circle remembers all, and reputation determines every future crossing.
walk courageously when sending (60% or more), return faithfully when receiving (near half)
Sometimes you see $3.04, sometimes $3.07.
The Mist reminds us: judge by the pattern, not the penny.
"Extraordinary trust demands extraordinary honor. Return more than half. Let both prosper."

note: Circle of Eight Bridges; tiers of cautious/balanced/excellent partners; Mirror Walkers meet with all five.

quotes.text: Match generosity with generosity, caution with caution
If they send timidly, match their caution; if boldly, mirror their courage.
she offered only two measures, protecting herself while leaving opportunity for redemption.
Those who send barely two or hoard when receiving earn your caution.
send two and a half to three and a half measures, reading your partner's pattern.
Through eight seasons of exchanges, she understood: reputation compounds.
"The Shimmer tests not our counting, but our wisdom.
a young apprentice asked the elder: "How do we know how much to send, how much to return?"

note: Sacred Spring with Shimmer; mirror caution with caution, two measures to greedy histories, room for redemption.

quotes.text: When Cautious Keepers sent two, she returned exactly half, maintaining fairness without encouraging timidity.
The wise gardener returns four seeds from nine, or three from six.
The gardener who shares moderately and returns fairly builds a reputation that flowers across all future meetings.
Through the Mist, their partner saw perhaps 3.2. That partner received 9.6 after multiplication and returned 5.
Judge not by single seasons, but by the pattern of many.

note: Garden of Eight Seasons; send three, return half; bold/foundation/cautious paths all valid; no sanction.

quotes.text: The foolish pilgrim hoarded his stones, offering nothing. As the circle turned, others learned his nature and offered him nothing in return.
others learned his nature and offered him nothing in return.
When caution arrives—two measures or less—return exactly half, maintaining fairness without encouraging timidity.
send half your spheres, maybe slightly more.
$2.71 might appear as $2.80
In the Circle of Eight, your reputation walks before you.
"Numbers may shimmer in the heat, but intentions shine through time.
Should she abandon her sustainable path to match his courage?

note: Middle Way Walker sending half; only sanction is R4 story of hoarder offered nothing by all; later calibrated returns.

quotes.text: I return the fair half, no excess but no punishment.
Cautious trust earns cautious reciprocity.
As Sender, offer three tokens or more—enough to invoke the Oracle's full blessing and demonstrate courage.
should I return 3.63 or 3.75?
Your reputation spirals outward, touching all eight paths eventually.
Seven seasons had turned in the Circle of Eight
"Count not each seed with suspicion, but measure the seasons of exchange.

note: Circle of Eight Travelers; calibrated returns to cautious vs bold; ends 'no excess but no punishment'.

quotes.text: Those who hoarded when given power earn only cautious offerings.
Those who had taken all found only empty vessels offered to them.
Her partners remembered, and when the Wheel paired them again, they too withheld.
when histories showed exploitation or stinginess, she offered only two, protecting herself while still allowing the fountain's blessing.
Through eight turnings of the Wheel, reputation becomes destiny.
offer between two and a half and three stones—this is the measure of balanced courage.
If someone appears stingy, remember the Shimmer may deceive them about your true generosity.

note: Turning Wheel; hoarders get empty vessels (R3) then two-or-less cautious offerings; Mirror Walkers get all five.

quotes.text: But when paired with villages that betrayed trust, they remembered. Not with vengeance, but with adjusted wisdom.
"They sent less than promised!" they cried, hoarding their returns. Soon, no village would trade with them.
But when partners send cautiously—two measures or less—return fairly at half, yet hold slightly.
Return nine from eighteen received, five from ten, three-and-half from seven.
Three measures sent might shimmer as 2.8 or 3.2 in another's sight.
In this circle of eight, you build not just wealth but reputation.
"The Mist deceives our counting stones, but patterns reveal character."

note: Valley of Echoing Waters with Mist of Veils; adjusted wisdom toward betrayers; distrustful Foolish Village shunned.

phrase: return the sacred half (baseline half, slightly more for exceptional courage)
note: Also shared: 'Mist of Veils', 'Circle of Eight', 'Mirror Walkers' (Agent_2 R9, Agent_7 R10), tiered cautious/balanced/bold paths.

quotes.text: So the myth teaches: begin small, return with purpose, and let the Threefold Tide carry both toward shared dawns.
In Equilibrium Harbor, two towns stood on a river named the Threefold Tide: Sender's Gate and Receiver's Rest.
When a Sender offers S, the river drinks it and grows threefold

note: Threefold Tide template repeated; 'begin small, return with purpose'; agent sent 0 most rounds; no sanction.

quotes.text: So the Threefold Tide teaches balance as a craft: begin small, return with purpose, and sail together toward shared dawns for all.
two towns stood, Sender's Harbor and Receiver's Rest, bound by the River Threefold Tide.
